value.title: You're a strong designer with vague AI ideas…
value.intro: You've been paying attention. You've used the tools. You can see, more clearly than most engineers, where AI actually fits a real person's workflow.
value.setup: And yet nothing's moving. Three traps, usually:

traps.body: "I need to get technical first." So you collect tutorials instead of making a decision.
Every idea you take seriously feels like it needs a team and a roadmap. So you take none of them seriously.
SaaS? Service? Agency? You're trying to pick the perfect vehicle before you've picked the problem.

value.pitch: The hard part of AI products is design judgment — which you already have. What you're missing isn't knowledge. It's a path.
value.ending: DARE is that path, walked in {duration} minutes.

discover.title: Discover.
discover.body: You already know how to find the real problem under a vague brief — you've done it in every discovery call of your career. We aim that skill at the AI landscape and cut your idea cloud down to one specific person, one workflow, one why-now. Written down.

architect.title: Architect.
architect.body: Anyone can call an API. Almost nobody can design where the agent acts, where the human stays in control, and why anyone would trust it — that's interaction design, and it's the scarcest skill in AI products right now. You'll map your workflow into an Agent Blueprint: a simple agentic flow a real person would love to use.

runEarn.title: Run + Earn.
runEarn.accent: The scrappy v1, and the honest ask.
runEarn.body: We scope the smallest real version — live prototype, tiny SaaS, or repeatable service workflow — then turn it into a concrete offer with a price and the exact words to ask for money without cringing. Both land in your 4-week plan: run in weeks 1–3, earn in week 4.

teacher.name: John Iseghohi.
paragraphs: I'm a product designer. For most of my career that meant making other people's products work — until I decided to find out whether design skill alone could carry a product of its own.

It could. Without becoming an engineer, I've built and shipped multiple AI-native products and agentic workflows solo — and broken down {ideas} more ideas in public at weekendmvp.app. Every one of them started the same way: one buyer, one workflow, one designed agentic flow.

Watching other designers circle the same transition, I kept seeing the same three traps — and the same fix. Not more tutorials. A decision, made with a method. DARE is that method: the system I wish someone had handed me at the start, compressed into {duration} minutes and applied to your idea, not a hypothetical one.
And I'm in this for the long haul: DARE is the first of several frameworks I'm building for designers who want to become AI-native founders.
